AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MARCH 15, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION
  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.8:
  Property: Alondra Library; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Negotiating
  Party: County of Los Angeles; Under Negotiation: Terms of Lease.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  April Reutter
  Pray Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Alexandria Rae Villanueva, 3rd grader
  William Orr Elementary

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize March as Women’s History Month in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim February 22 as “Penny Brother’s Day" in the City of Norwalk in honor of
  Elijhaa and Rashaad Penny for their individual successes and contributions to the Norwalk community.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Emanuel Salazar, 8th grade student, to share his book “Letters to the President.”

  3.  Recognition of Sergeant Foster and Deputy Conger for their Service to Norwalk.

  4.  Recognition of Sergeant Pena and Public Safety Officer Warren for their Outstanding Arrest and Aide to
  a Homeless Individual.

  5.  Community Clean-up Event video.

  6.  Meet the Mayor video.

  7.  Week in Review video.
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of
  February 22, March 1, and 8, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period February 6, –
  February 19, 2022, in the total amount of $945,227.75. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  February 25, – March 9, 2022 in the total amount of $3,462,397.80. 640

  Warrant Register

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Anthony
  Adame and Angel Ronquillo. 830-01/

  Report

  5.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  6.  PROJECT NO. 7377 – ACCEPT WORK FOR INSTALLATION OF NEW PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT
  AT HOLIFIELD PARK - Staff recommends City Council accept the work of Landscape Structures Inc.
  for the installation of playground equipment at Holifield Park in the amount of $ 369,851.66. 1004-05-
  7377

  Report

  7.  ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR PROJECT NOS. 7924.1/.3 - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION
  PROGRAM PAVING IMPROVEMENTS IN ZONE 24; 7185 – SHOEMAKER AVENUE; AND 7798 –
  TRANSIT CENTER PARKING LOT - RESOLUTION NO. 22-17 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-17, RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE MEASURE M BOND FUNDS FOR PROJECT NO. 7924 – LOCAL
  STREETS REHABILITATION PROGRAM CONCRETE AND PAVING IMPROVEMENTS – ZONE
  24, in the amount of $175,000;

  b.  accept the work of CJ Concrete, in the amount of $855,164.64 for Project No. 7924.1 Local Street
  Rehabilitation Program paving improvements and for Project No. 7185 Shoemaker Avenue
  Improvements;

  c.  accept the work of All American Asphalt, in the amount of $202,114.52, for Project No. 7924.3,
  Local Street Rehabilitation Program paving improvements; and

  d.  accept the work of All American Asphalt, in the amount of $32,897.72, for Project No. 7798,
  Transit Center Parking Lot. 610/1004-05-7924.1/7924.3/7798
   Report

  8.  PROJECT NO. 7925.3 - ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM -
  PAVING IMPROVEMENTS IN ZONE 27 - Staff recommends City Council accept the work of All
  American Asphalt, in the amount of $1,150,092.62, for Project No. 7925.3, Local Street Rehabilitation
  Program paving improvements. 1004-05-7925.3

  Report

  9.  PROJECT NO. 7926.3 - ACCEPTANCE OF WORK - LOCAL STREET REHABILITATION PROGRAM
  PAVING IMPROVEMENTS IN ZONE 32 - Staff recommends City Council accept the work of Sully-
  Miller Contracting Company, in the amount of $640,504.36 for Project No. 7926.3, Local Street
  Rehabilitation Program paving improvements. 1004-05-7926.3

  Report

  10. REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR PRAY NORWALK EVENT - Staff recommends
  City Council approve the carnival requested by Pray Norwalk for the date of Saturday, June 4, 2022
  and waive the security deposit as requested consistent with past practice.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  12. PROPOSED ACTIVITIES FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS
  PROGRAM - The City Council and the public is requested to provide input of the proposed CDBG and
  HOME funding activities for Fiscal Year 2022/23 Annual Action Plan. RESOLUTION

  Report

REPORTS

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 22-18 – FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 BUDGET AMENDMENT FOR PRIORITIZED
  PARK PROJECTS – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-18, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING AMENDMENTS TO THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2021/22 BUDGET FOR PRIORITIZED PARK PROJECTS; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute any contracts and amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City,
  in a form approved by the City Attorney.

  Report

  14. APPROVAL OF CITY SPEED HUMP POLICY - Staff recommends City Council approve the Speed
  Hump policy.

  Report

  15. THE 2021 NORWALK GENERAL PLAN AND HOUSING ELEMENT ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT -
  Staff recommends City Council receive and file the 2021 General Plan and Housing Element Annual
  Progress Report, and direct staff to forward a copy of the report to the Governor’s Office of Planning
  and Research and the State Department of Housing and Community Development prior to April 1,
  2022.

  Report

  16. PARKING ACTION PLAN AND LICENSE PLATE READER HARDWARE AND SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council:
   a.  approve the proposed Parking Action Plan recommendations for the Preferential Parking Zone
  application process and direct staff to prepare an ordinance for the next City Council meeting
  amending Chapter 10.08 of Title 10 of the Norwalk Municipal Code to incorporate the new process
  from the Parking Action Plan; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute an agreement with Vigilant Solutions for license plate
  reader hardware and services in an amount not to exceed $55,000 and any amendments,
  provided that there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
  Attorney.

  Report

  17. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – MARCH EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive
  and file.

  Report

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated March 11, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
